text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Australian boxer LARRY FOLEY, who became a national champion, was born in 1849.
West Australian journalist and humorist EDWIN MURPHY was born in 1866. He wrote song lyrics for "Hands Across The Sea" and "We've Got A Big Brother in America".
Respected American film actor EDWARD G. ROBINSON was born in 1893. He was the menacing heavy in films such as "Little Caesar" and "Key Largo".
Australian timber merchant CHARLES HARDY, who led a Riverina secessionist movement, was born in 1898.

Ol' Blue Eyes FRANK SINATRA gave his vocal chords their first workout when he was born in 1915. The singer and film actor is particularly associated with the song "My Way". His films from 1941 included "From Here To Eternity" (1953) and "Guys and Dolls" (1955).

US singer CONNIE FRANCIS (CONCETTA ROSA MARIA FRANCONERA) was born in 1938. She made her first record in 1955 and was successful from 1957. Hits included "Who's Sorry Now"(1958), "My Happiness"(1958), "Lipstick On Your Collar"(1959) and "Everybody's Somebody's Fool"(1960). After she was raped in 1974 CONNIE withdrew from show business to stage a comeback in 1978.

American singer DIONNE WARWICK, who began as a gospel singer, was born in 1940. She sang with her sister DEE DEE and her aunt CISSY HOUSTON (mother of WHITNEY) as the 'Gospelaires'. She was discovered by song writing team BACHARACH/DAVID who considered DIONNE's voice to be suitable for their compositions. Her hits included "Walk On By"(1964), "I Say A Little Prayer"(1967), "I'll Never Love This Way Again"(1979) and "Heartbreaker"(1982).

US jazz/funk saxophonist and songwriter GROVER WASHINGTON Junior was born in 1943. At the age of 16 he had his own band - the 'Four Clefs'. After that he worked as a session musician and soloist. His greatest hit was sung by BILL WITHERS "Just The Two Of Us"(1981).
Brazilian motor-racing champion EMMERSON FITTIPALDI was born in 1946.
** EVENTS **
1900 : The British War Office announced that more than
11,000 troops had been killed in the Boer War. 1901 : The Atlantic Ocean was bridged by the miracle of

wireless. Italian inventor GUGLIELMO MARCONI sent a wireless signal across the Atlantic Ocean with his radio wave apparatus. The breakthrough was applauded on both sides of the Atlantic by those who could see the benefits of instant long-distance communication without the need for telegraph wires.
1907 : In New York a rule was introduced forcing women to
sign affidavits attesting to their age and good character.
1913 : The "Mona Lisa" - LEONARDO DA VINCI'S famous

painting was found, two years after being stolen from the Louvre in Paris. It was discovered hidden under a bed in a small Florence hotel. Italian housepainter VINCENZO PERUGGIA stole the painting because he was incensed by French chauvinism.
1924 : Almost 400 lots went up for sale in the first land
sale in Canberra. The auctioneer predicted 10,000 people would be living in the area within ten years.
1932 : The USSR restored relations with Japan.
1955 : British electronic engineer CHRISTOPHER COCKERELL
patented his new vehicle. The half-ship, half-aircraft "hovercraft" floated on a cushion of air produced by fans and was pushed forward by air propellers.
1978 : More than 340 people were arrested in a wild

demonstration in Brisbane as 1,500 people protested against Queensland's law against street marches. Violence broke out between the 1,200 police and the protestors as they moved out of King George Square into Albert Street. Among those arrested were Labor MP TOM UREN, Senator GEORGE GEORGES and ACTU vice-president JOHN DUCKER. Queensland premier JOH BJELKE-PETERSEN described the protest as "futile".
1982 : More than 20,000 British women linked hands around

Greenham Common airbase in a protest against US plans to site a nuclear cruise missile at the base. The protest began four months ago when the women set up camp at the base. Several had been jailed but despite this the protest continued.
1988 : British rock star ELTON JOHN was awarded damages
of 1.85 million dollars against the "Sun" newspaper for its libellous allegations about his private life.
1989 : New York billionairess LEONA HELMSLEY was fined

seven million dollars and sentenced to four months jail for tax evasion. She had been convicted of evading more than one million dollars in tax. She was once quoted as saying "Only little people pay taxes".
1990 : United States president GEORGE BUSH agreed to send
a 1000 million dollar food aid package to the Soviet Union.
1991 : The Russian parliament voted overwhelmingly in
favour of replacing the Soviet Union with a loose Commonwealth of Independent States.
1994 : Sydney roadworker, 49-year-old IVAN MILAT, was
committed to stand trial over the so-called backpacker murders in the Belanglo State Forest in southern New South Wales.
